sources: What matters next: Evidence that Resulticks' customer base is adopting the broader platform (cross-sell traction), and that revenue growth from the combined entity is accelerating faster than the cost of integration.
prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage: bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design, photographed flat under soft room light.
2. One flat block-colour paper ground fills the frame: lime green. The ground is a single unbroken colour.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Every cutout is a plain, unmarked object: calendar pages, documents, coins, screens and vehicles are blank and unprinted, with no lettering, numerals, symbols, liveries or marks on them. Every cutout is matte paper reflecting only the room light, with a plain blank face: coin rims, document faces, screens and vehicle sides carry no lettering, numerals or marks.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons, tape, rubber stamps, string and pins, stencilled arrows, paper bar charts, stacked sheets, grid paper, torn strips, hole-punched tags, paper clips, in cream, black, pale yellow or the ground's contrasting colour, with real paper texture and print dots.
5. One consistent light from the upper left; each paper layer casts a small soft shadow.
6. Layout: the headline chip owns the upper third of the frame and stays uncovered; subjects and diagrams occupy the lower two-thirds. When the frame opens on a previous composition, its elements slide off or are covered in the first second and the new headline lands on clear ground.
7. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif in black or cream, printed on a cream or black paper chip: one line, no wider than a third of the frame width, with safe margins, the chip sitting clear of the subjects. Letterforms are accurate, complete and stable from the frame they appear in; the chip is printed once and does not redraw. When the beat marks a hero number, that number alone may be printed larger, up to half the frame width.
8. Compositions vary in scale from beat to beat: some show one oversized subject filling the frame, some a small subject alone on open ground, some several elements arranged as a diagram.
9. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window; one strongest focus at a time; the camera is locked; movement starts on the first frame and a small loop continues at the end; no empty frames.
10. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
11. Identity anchor: rough white torn edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from the upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: lime green.
Subjects: a paper calendar page; a stencilled arrow.
Opens on the clipped files, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: The previous chip flips away as the clipped files fan into a paper calendar page; a stencilled arrow climbs across it and holds at the edge.
Ends holding on the climbing arrow.
This composition is a diagram: several elements are arranged together.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "CROSS-SELL PROOF".

ON-SCREEN TEXT: "CROSS-SELL PROOF". This string is printed complete and correct from its first visible frame and never changes. It is the only lettering in the frame.

AUDIO: One English narrator, warm, clear, natural, brisk but unhurried, never an advertising shout. Speak the following line exactly once, word for word, beginning on the first frame: "What matters next is cross-sell traction and faster revenue growth.". No other dialogue. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects beneath the voice; no music.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] This is a modern editorial paper collage, photographed as a flat lay under soft room light from the upper left. The scene opens on <Picture 1>, featuring a magenta paper ground with a cream paper chip reading "G&A $8.1M" and a bar chart made of cream paper strips. Immediately, the magenta ground is covered by a single, unbroken block of lime green matte paper. Simultaneously, the previous headline chip flips away rapidly with a slight overshoot, and the cream bar chart elements fan out and transform into a single, black-and-white halftone photographic cutout of a paper calendar page. The calendar page is unmarked, blank, and features rough white torn-paper edges, casting a small soft shadow to the bottom right. A new cream paper chip lands in the upper third of the frame, featuring the stable, extra-bold sans-serif black text "CROSS-SELL PROOF", which remains legible and unchanged. A flat matte paper stencilled arrow in black then slides quickly across the surface of the blank calendar page, climbing upward and coming to a stable hold at the right edge. The camera remains in a Static Shot throughout the 5 seconds. A male narrator (S1), with a warm, clear, and brisk professional timbre, speaks throughout the action: <d>[English] What matters next is cross-sell traction and faster revenue growth.</d>

overall_soundscape: The audio is dominated by the crisp, tactile sounds of a paper-based environment. Audible elements include the sharp "slap" of paper landing on a surface, the subtle frictional slide of a paper cutout moving across the ground, and the light, sticky sound of tape being pressed down.
